### **Claude** `02:57`

# SYSTEM OVERVIEW

The Automotive Parts Arbitrage Intelligence Platform (codename **APAX-INTEL**) is a production-grade, multi-agent OSINT and operational analytics system designed to supervise the continuous extraction, normalization, deduplication, enrichment, and demand-correlation of automotive spare parts inventory sourced from Spanish desguaces, dismantlers, breakers, and salvage yards. The platform fuses high-frequency scraping signals, AI-driven entity normalization, geographic supply intelligence, and pan-European demand telemetry into a single tactical workstation.

The front-end is not a consumer application. It is an **operational intelligence cockpit** built for OSINT analysts, inventory engineers, arbitrage strategists, AI agent supervisors, and automation operators who require sub-second interaction latency over inventories spanning 1M+ SKUs across hundreds of yards. The visual language draws from Bloomberg Terminal information density, Palantir Gotham investigative graph workflows, and automotive industrial HMI conventions (think TRW, Bosch DAS, fleet TMS consoles).

The system operates under three primary supervisory loops:

| Loop | Cadence | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Extraction Supervision** | Sub-second to minute | Monitor crawlers, parsers, normalizers, validators across hundreds of source yards |
| **Inventory Intelligence** | Minute to hourly | Track SKU freshness, deduplication, OEM cross-reference, compatibility lineage |
| **Arbitrage Correlation** | Hourly to daily | Match Spanish supply against European demand to surface high-margin opportunities |

The dashboard is the **human-in-the-loop control surface** of an otherwise autonomous agent network. It must degrade gracefully under load, support multi-monitor 4K workflows, and remain keyboard-driven for power users. Every interaction must be auditable; every screen must support drill-down to raw extraction lineage; every visualization must be exportable to downstream BI and ERP pipelines.

# CORE OPERATIONAL OBJECTIVES

The platform's operational mandate is decomposed into seven non-negotiable objectives, ordered by priority:

1. **Supply Visibility at Scale** — Provide a unified, queryable, real-time view of every part exposed by every monitored yard, with provenance, freshness, and confidence metadata at the row level. Target: 1M+ active SKUs, 500+ active yards, p95 query latency < 250ms.
2. **Agent Fleet Observability** — Render the state, throughput, error budget, token consumption, queue depth, and confidence distribution of every running agent (crawler, extractor, parser, normalizer, enricher, validator, deduper) in real time.
3. **Demand-Supply Coincidence Detection** — Continuously correlate Spanish inventory against German, French, Italian, UK, and Benelux demand signals (marketplace queries, OEM stockouts, eBay Motors trends, RockAuto gaps, manheim auction signals) to surface arbitrage windows.
4. **Entity Normalization Integrity** — Guarantee canonical resolution of part identities across heterogeneous taxonomies (manufacturer SKU, OEM reference, aftermarket cross-ref, free-text descriptions, VIN-linked groupings).
5. **Operational Auditability** — Every datum on screen must trace back to (a) the source yard, (b) the extraction agent, (c) the parse confidence, (d) the normalization decision, (e) the dedup cluster head.
6. **Latency-Aware Decision Making** — Surface time-sensitive arbitrage windows with explicit decay indicators (a part listed 3 days ago is worth less signal than one listed 30 minutes ago).
7. **Pipeline Export Discipline** — All filtered, faceted, or correlated views must be one-keystroke exportable to CSV, Parquet, JSON-LD, and direct ERP/marketplace push channels.

Secondary objectives include multi-tenant separation (per-operator workspaces), regulatory traceability (GDPR-aware extraction logs), and graceful capability degradation when upstream agents fail.

# INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE

The IA is organized as a **three-tier navigational hierarchy**: Workspace → Module → Object Inspector. Modules are top-level operational surfaces; Object Inspectors are right-rail or modal drill-downs that preserve module context.

```
┌── WORKSPACE LAYER ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│   Top bar: Org switcher | Workspace | Env (prod/staging) | Cmd+K │
├── MODULE LAYER ────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│   Left rail (collapsible, icon+label):                          │
│     • Global Dashboard                                          │
│     • Scrap Yard Explorer                                       │
│     • Inventory Index Viewer                                    │
│     • Parts Intelligence Panel                                  │
│     • Supply vs Demand                                          │
│     • Geographic Heatmap                                        │
│     • Agent Activity Monitor                                    │
│     • Scraping Health Monitor                                   │
│     • Inventory Freshness Tracker                               │
│     • Arbitrage Opportunity Center                              │
│     • Search & Semantic Query                                   │
│     • Duplicate Detection Panel                                 │
│     • Entity Normalization System                               │
│     • Marketplace Correlation                                   │
│     • Export & Pipeline Console                                 │
├── OBJECT INSPECTOR LAYER ──────────────────────────────────────┤
│   Right rail (resizable, pinnable):                             │
│     • Yard Detail | Part Detail | Agent Detail                  │
│     • Arbitrage Card | Lineage Trace | Export Spec              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**URL Schema** (preserves deep-linkability and shareable state):

```
/w/:workspace/m/:module/v/:viewId?q=<encoded-query>&filters=<facet-state>&inspect=<entityId>
```

**Persistence Strategy**: workspace state, pinned filters, saved queries, layout breakpoints, and inspector pin state are all serialized to `localStorage` keyed by workspace+user, with optional cloud sync via a `/api/preferences` endpoint. Tab-restoration uses URL state as source of truth; localStorage is the fallback.

**Cross-module breadcrumbs** are emitted via a global `NavigationContext` so that, e.g., clicking a yard in the Heatmap deep-links to Scrap Yard Explorer with that yard pre-selected and the inspector pre-opened.

# PRIMARY MODULES

| # | Module | Primary User | Cadence | Density |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Global Dashboard** | Ops Lead, CEO | Live | Mixed (KPI + sparkline + alert feed) |
| 2 | **Scrap Yard Explorer** | OSINT Analyst | Live | High (table + map + cards) |
| 3 | **Inventory Index Viewer** | Inventory Engineer | Live | Maximum (virtualized table 1M+) |
| 4 | **Parts Intelligence Panel** | Arbitrage Researcher | Hourly | Mixed (graph + table + facets) |
| 5 | **Supply vs Demand Correlation Engine** | Arbitrage Strategist | Live | High (matrix + scoring + alerts) |
| 6 | **Geographic Heatmap** | Logistics Analyst | Live | Visual (map + choropleth + cluster) |
| 7 | **Agent Activity Monitor** | AI Supervisor | Sub-second | Maximum (log stream + metrics) |
| 8 | **Scraping Health Monitor** | DevOps / Platform | Sub-second | High (status grid + error budget) |
| 9 | **Inventory Freshness Tracker** | Inventory Engineer | Live | High (decay curves + heat strips) |
| 10 | **Arbitrage Opportunity Center** | Arbitrage Strategist | Live | Mixed (ranked cards + spread bars) |
| 11 | **Search & Semantic Query System** | All operators | Interactive | Mixed (query bar + result table) |
| 12 | **Duplicate Detection Panel** | Inventory Engineer | Live | High (cluster viewer + merge UI) |
| 13 | **Entity Normalization System** | Data Engineer | Live | High (mapping table + rule editor) |
| 14 | **Marketplace Correlation View** | Arbitrage Researcher | Hourly | High (cross-source table) |
| 15 | **Export & Pipeline Console** | Integration Engineer | On-demand | Mixed (pipeline graph + queue) |

Each module is a code-split route, lazy-loaded with a Suspense boundary, and instrumented with module-level telemetry (mount time, first interaction, p95 panel render).

# SCREEN-BY-SCREEN SPECIFICATION

## 1. Global Dashboard
- **Purpose**: Single-pane situational awareness for the entire arbitrage operation.
- **Primary User**: Ops Lead, CEO, Aurelius (audit agent).
- **Key Panels**:
  - **Supply KPI strip**: Total SKUs, active yards, 24h new listings, dedup ratio.
  - **Agent fleet status**: heatgrid of agent classes × status.
  - **Arbitrage P&L sparkline**: realized vs surfaced opportunities, 7d/30d.
  - **Live alert feed**: agent failures, scarcity spikes, demand surges.
  - **Freshness gauge**: % inventory < 24h old, < 7d, < 30d, stale.
  - **Geo mini-map**: aggregated yard heat over Iberian peninsula.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/metrics/global`, WS `events:global`, WS `alerts:critical`.
- **Key CTAs**: "Jump to opportunity #X", "Acknowledge alert", "Pin KPI to workspace".
- **Alerts/State**: critical alerts cause top-bar pulse + sound (opt-in); module-level error bars on data staleness > 60s.
- **Links**: every panel deep-links into its module (KPI → Inventory Viewer, agent grid → Agent Monitor, geo mini-map → Heatmap).

## 2. Scrap Yard Explorer
- **Purpose**: Catalogue, filter, and inspect every monitored yard entity.
- **Primary User**: OSINT Analyst, Inventory Engineer.
- **Key Panels**:
  - Master table (virtualized, ~500-2000 rows): name, region, operational scale, est. inventory volume, supported brands (chip cluster), categories, exposed inventory systems (e.g., MotorNet, B-Parts, eCarParts, OEM internal, custom HTML), inventory freshness gauge, contact/public metadata, extraction confidence, sync status.
  - Card grid mode (toggle): poster-style cards for visual triage.
  - Right-rail Yard Inspector: full provenance, agent assignments, extraction logs, robots.txt status, last successful crawl, schema fingerprint.
  - Map overlay (collapsible): yards plotted with size = inventory volume.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/yards`, `/api/yards/:id`, WS `events:yard-sync`.
- **Key CTAs**: "Force re-crawl", "Pause agent", "Open in Inventory Viewer filtered by this yard", "Export yard sheet".
- **Alerts/State**: red strip on yards with extraction confidence < 0.7; amber strip on freshness > 7d; offline icon on yards failing 3+ consecutive crawls.
- **Links**: Yard → Inventory Viewer (filtered), Yard → Agent Monitor (filtered), Yard → Heatmap (focused).

## 3. Inventory Index Viewer
- **Purpose**: The primary high-density part exploration surface.
- **Primary User**: Inventory Engineer, Arbitrage Researcher.
- **Key Panels**:
  - **Virtualized table** (TanStack Table + Virtual, 1M+ rows): part name, OEM ref, manufacturer SKU, donor VIN, category, condition (A/B/C/scrap), price, currency, yard, listed_at, last_seen, freshness chip, dedup cluster ID, confidence.
  - **Faceted filter sidebar**: brand, model, year range, category tree, condition, price range, region, freshness window, has-VIN, has-OEM-ref.
  - **Semantic query bar**: natural language + structured DSL (`brand:BMW model:E46 cat:engine cond:>=B fresh:<7d`).
  - **Row inspector**: full lineage trace, compatibility tree, dedup siblings, marketplace cross-refs.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/inventory/search` (paginated), `/api/parts/:id`, WS `events:inventory-delta`.
- **Key CTAs**: "Add to opportunity list", "Mark as duplicate", "Override normalization", "Export selection", "Push to ERP".
- **Alerts/State**: row badges for dedup conflicts, normalization low-confidence, price anomaly (z-score > 2.5).
- **Links**: Part → Parts Intelligence, Part → Marketplace Correlation, Part → Dedup Panel (cluster view).

## 4. Parts Intelligence Panel
- **Purpose**: Deep semantic exploration of a single part identity across yards, time, and marketplaces.
- **Primary User**: Arbitrage Researcher.
- **Key Panels**:
  - Canonical part header: OEM ref, all aliases, compatible vehicle graph.
  - **Compatibility graph** (force-directed, cytoscape.js): part → vehicles → years → trims.
  - Price history chart (ECharts line + candlestick) across yards and marketplaces.
  - Source list with confidence and freshness.
  - Dedup cluster panel showing alternate listings.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/parts/:canonicalId/intel`.
- **Key CTAs**: "Watch this part", "Create arbitrage rule", "Override compatibility".
- **Links**: → Marketplace Correlation, → Arbitrage Center.

## 5. Supply vs Demand Correlation Engine
- **Purpose**: Surface high-signal coincidences between Spanish supply and European demand.
- **Primary User**: Arbitrage Strategist.
- **Key Panels**:
  - **Correlation matrix** (heatmap): rows = part categories, cols = demand regions, cell color = opportunity score.
  - **Opportunity feed**: ranked, with spread, confidence, decay timer.
  - **Demand source legend**: eBay Motors, mobile.de parts, leboncoin, Allegro, AutoScout24 parts, RockAuto out-of-stock signals.
  - **Scoring breakdown sidebar**: weights, signal contributions, expected margin.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/correlation/matrix`, `/api/opportunities`, WS `events:opportunity-new`.
- **Key CTAs**: "Promote to Arbitrage Center", "Snooze", "Investigate signal".
- **Alerts/State**: pulse on opportunities with score > 0.85; gray-out on decayed (>72h).
- **Links**: → Arbitrage Opportunity Center, → Marketplace Correlation.

## 6. Geographic Heatmap
- **Purpose**: Spatial intelligence on supply density and arbitrage gradients.
- **Primary User**: Logistics Analyst.
- **Key Panels**:
  - **MapLibre GL canvas** (Iberian Peninsula default zoom, pan to EU):
    - Yard markers clustered (Supercluster).
    - Choropleth overlay: SKU density per NUTS-3 region.
    - Toggle layers: freshness, brand specialization, agent health.
  - Side legend with filter chips.
  - Region inspector: aggregate stats on hover/click.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/geo/yards`, `/api/geo/density`, vector tiles for NUTS boundaries.
- **Key CTAs**: "Filter inventory by region", "Export region report".
- **Links**: → Scrap Yard Explorer (regional filter), → Inventory Viewer.

## 7. Agent Activity Monitor
- **Purpose**: Real-time observability of every running agent.
- **Primary User**: AI Supervisor, DevOps.
- **Key Panels**:
  - **Agent grid**: each cell = one agent instance, color = state (idle/running/erroring/throttled).
  - **Live log stream** (SSE-backed, virtualized log viewer).
  - **Per-agent metrics panel**: queue depth, throughput (parts/min), success rate, token usage, p95 latency, confidence distribution histogram.
  - **Failure diagnostics**: last 100 errors with stack, payload snippet, suggested action.
- **Data Sources**: WS `events:agent-state`, SSE `/api/agents/:id/logs`, `/api/agents/metrics`.
- **Key CTAs**: "Restart", "Drain queue", "Adjust concurrency", "View source schema".
- **Alerts/State**: agent in error >5min → red; token budget >80% → amber.
- **Links**: → Scraping Health Monitor, → Yard Explorer (agent's assigned yard).

## 8. Scraping Health Monitor
- **Purpose**: System-wide scraping reliability and error budget tracking.
- **Primary User**: DevOps, Platform Engineer.
- **Key Panels**:
  - Source status grid (yard × status).
  - Error budget burndown (SLO: 99.5% success).
  - Anti-bot detection events feed.
  - Schema drift alerts (Yard X changed HTML structure).
- **Data Sources**: `/api/health/scraping`, WS `events:schema-drift`.
- **Key CTAs**: "Open schema diff", "Pause source", "Acknowledge drift".
- **Links**: → Agent Monitor, → Yard Explorer.

## 9. Inventory Freshness Tracker
- **Purpose**: Quantify and visualize SKU decay across yards.
- **Primary User**: Inventory Engineer.
- **Key Panels**:
  - **Heat strips** per yard: rows = yards, columns = time buckets (last 24h hourly, then daily 7d, then weekly 30d), cell color = % fresh.
  - Decay curve per category.
  - Stale SKU table (>30d unseen → likely sold/removed).
- **Data Sources**: `/api/freshness/yards`, `/api/freshness/categories`.
- **Key CTAs**: "Trigger refresh crawl", "Mark stale as removed".

## 10. Arbitrage Opportunity Center
- **Purpose**: The operator's daily action queue.
- **Primary User**: Arbitrage Strategist.
- **Key Panels**:
  - Ranked opportunity cards: part image, supply yard, demand region, buy price, expected sell, spread €, margin %, confidence, decay timer.
  - Filter rail: min spread, min margin, min confidence, category, region.
  - Selected card detail: supply provenance, demand evidence, logistics estimate, risk flags.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/opportunities/ranked`.
- **Key CTAs**: "Claim", "Push to ERP", "Dismiss with reason", "Create automation rule".
- **Alerts/State**: card pulse on confidence > 0.9; gray-out on claimed-by-other-operator (presence-aware).
- **Links**: → Parts Intelligence, → Marketplace Correlation.

## 11. Search & Semantic Query System
- **Purpose**: Cross-module unified search.
- **Primary User**: All operators.
- **Key Panels**:
  - Global query bar (Cmd+K).
  - Faceted result list: parts, yards, agents, opportunities.
  - Saved queries panel.
  - DSL helper / autocomplete.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/search` (Meilisearch or Typesense backed).
- **Key CTAs**: "Save query", "Subscribe to query (alerts)", "Export results".

## 12. Duplicate Detection Panel
- **Purpose**: Manage dedup clusters and resolve ambiguities.
- **Primary User**: Inventory Engineer.
- **Key Panels**:
  - Cluster list: candidate clusters with similarity score, member count, source diversity.
  - Cluster detail: side-by-side member comparison, image grid, attribute diff table.
  - Manual merge/split UI.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/dedup/clusters`, `/api/dedup/clusters/:id`.
- **Key CTAs**: "Confirm cluster", "Split member", "Promote canonical".

## 13. Entity Normalization System
- **Purpose**: Maintain canonical taxonomies (brands, models, categories, OEM refs).
- **Primary User**: Data Engineer.
- **Key Panels**:
  - Mapping table: raw → canonical with confidence.
  - Rule editor (DSL or visual): regex, ML-suggested mappings.
  - Conflict queue: ambiguous mappings needing human review.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/normalization/mappings`, `/api/normalization/rules`.

## 14. Marketplace Correlation View
- **Purpose**: Compare a part's appearance across European marketplaces.
- **Primary User**: Arbitrage Researcher.
- **Key Panels**:
  - Cross-source table: marketplace × price × stock × seller rating × shipping.
  - Spread visualization.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/marketplace/parts/:canonicalId`.

## 15. Export & Pipeline Console
- **Purpose**: Manage outbound data flows.
- **Primary User**: Integration Engineer.
- **Key Panels**:
  - Pipeline DAG view (React Flow): source → transform → destination.
  - Export queue.
  - Scheduled export calendar.
  - Destination configs: ERP, Shopify, eBay, custom webhooks.
- **Data Sources**: `/api/pipelines`, WS `events:pipeline-run`.

# COMPONENT SYSTEM

The component system follows a **strict atomic hierarchy** with composability and accessibility as primary constraints. All components are built atop Radix UI primitives, styled with Tailwind CSS, variant-managed via `class-variance-authority` (CVA), and documented in a Storybook instance.

## Atomic Tiers

| Tier | Example | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| **0 — Tokens** | Color, spacing, type, radius, motion | Defined in `tokens.ts`, consumed via Tailwind config |
| **1 — Primitives** | Button, Input, Checkbox, Tooltip, Popover | Unstyled Radix wrapped with CVA variants |
| **2 — Compounds** | TableCell, FacetChip, KPIStat, AgentStatusDot, ConfidenceBar | Built from primitives |
| **3 — Modules** | VirtualizedDataTable, FacetSidebar, LogStream, MapCanvas, CorrelationMatrix | Tier-2 + business logic hooks |
| **4 — Screens** | YardExplorerScreen, ArbitrageCenterScreen | Composed modules per route |

## Catalogue (selected)

```
<DataTable />              // TanStack Table + Virtual wrapper, density-aware
<FacetSidebar />           // Collapsible faceted filter UI
<EntityCard />             // Yard/Part/Agent unified card shell
<EntityInspector />        // Right-rail drill-down container
<StatusDot />              // 6-state agent/yard health indicator
<ConfidenceBar />          // 0–1 confidence with color thresholds
<FreshnessChip />          // Time-bucketed freshness pill
<SparklineCell />          // Inline mini-chart for table rows
<KPICard />                // Headline + delta + sparkline
<HeatStrip />              // Horizontal time-bucket heat row
<LogViewer />              // Virtualized SSE log stream
<MapCanvas />              // MapLibre GL React wrapper
<CorrelationMatrix />      // Categorical heatmap with click-through
<OpportunityCard />        // Ranked arbitrage card
<LineageTrace />           // Provenance walker (yard→agent→parse→norm→dedup)
<SchemaDiffViewer />       // HTML structural diff
<CommandPalette />         // Cmd+K command surface
<PresenceAvatars />        // Multi-operator presence overlay
<ExportSpecBuilder />      // Drag-and-drop export config
<DedupClusterViewer />     // Cluster comparison grid
```

## Variant Discipline

Every component declares variants explicitly via CVA. Example:

```ts
const statusDot = cva('inline-block rounded-full', {
  variants: {
    state: {
      idle:      'bg-zinc-500',
      running:   'bg-emerald-500 animate-pulse-slow',
      throttled: 'bg-amber-500',
      erroring:  'bg-red-500 animate-pulse',
      offline:   'bg-zinc-700 ring-1 ring-zinc-600',
      unknown:   'bg-zinc-600 ring-1 ring-dashed',
    },
    size: { xs: 'h-1.5 w-1.5', sm: 'h-2 w-2', md: 'h-3 w-3' },
  },
  defaultVariants: { state: 'unknown', size: 'sm' },
});
```

## Accessibility

- Every interactive component must pass WCAG 2.1 AA on the dark theme.
- Focus rings: 2px solid `--focus-ring` (#5EA0FF) with 2px offset.
- All tables expose ARIA grid semantics.
- Keyboard shortcuts registered via central `useShortcut(scope, keys, handler)` to avoid collisions.

# INVENTORY VISUALIZATION ENGINE

The Inventory Visualization Engine (IVE) is the single most performance-critical subsystem. It must render and interact with **1M+ rows** without UI thread stalls.

## Architecture

```
                ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
                │  TanStack Query (server cache)          │
                │  - cursor pagination                    │
                │  - background refetch on WS delta       │
                └──────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                               │
                ┌──────────────▼──────────────────────────┐
                │  IVE Core (custom hook: useInventory)   │
                │  - normalizes rows                      │
                │  - applies client-side facets           │
                │  - delegates heavy ops to Web Worker    │
                └──────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                               │
                ┌──────────────▼──────────────────────────┐
                │  TanStack Table v8                      │
                │  + @tanstack/react-virtual               │
                │  - columnVirtualizer + rowVirtualizer   │
                │  - column resizing, pinning, grouping   │
                └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Capabilities

| Capability | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Row virtualization | `@tanstack/react-virtual` with overscan=10, dynamic height fallback for expanded rows |
| Column virtualization | Horizontal virtualizer enabled when columns > 20 |
| Clustered category trees | Left-side tree built from materialized hierarchy; click filters table |
| Semantic filtering | DSL parser (chevrotain) translates `brand:BMW cat:engine cond:>=B` to query AST |
| Faceted filtering | Server returns facet counts alongside results; client merges into FacetSidebar |
| VIN-linked grouping | Group-by donor VIN collapses N parts under one vehicle row |
| OEM reference indexing | Secondary index in Meilisearch; cross-yard joins on OEM ref |
| Compatibility systems | Compatibility graph stored as canonical part → vehicle-trim-year edges; UI surfaces it on row expand |
| Lineage tracking | Each row carries `_lineage_id`; inspector fetches full provenance on demand |

## UI Primitives (row-level)

| Primitive | Visual |
|---|---|
| `<CategoryChip>` | Icon + canonical category label, color-coded by major class (powertrain, body, electronics, suspension, interior) |
| `<ConditionBadge>` | A/B/C/D grade with tooltip explaining grading rubric |
| `<StockStatusDot>` | available / reserved / sold / removed |
| `<DonorVehicleLink>` | VIN-shortened with hover popover showing full vehicle metadata |
| `<CompatibilityCount>` | Count of compatible vehicles, click expands to graph |
| `<PriceCell>` | Price + currency + delta vs 30d median + anomaly flag |
| `<FreshnessChip>` | "12m", "3h", "2d", "14d" with color decay from emerald → zinc |
| `<DedupChip>` | Cluster size + canonical indicator (★ on canonical row) |
| `<ConfidenceBar>` | 0–1 horizontal bar, red <0.5, amber <0.8, emerald ≥0.8 |

## Density Modes

| Mode | Row height | Font | Use case |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compact | 28px | 11px | High-throughput triage, 4K monitors |
| Comfortable | 36px | 12px | Default analyst work |
| Expanded | 56px | 13px | Detailed inspection with inline sparklines |

Density is a workspace-level preference, overridable per session via `Cmd+Shift+D`.

# AI AGENT MONITORING SYSTEM

The Agent Monitor exposes the autonomous agent fleet as a **fully observable distributed system**. Every agent emits a standardized telemetry envelope; the UI subscribes via websocket and renders state transitions in real time.

## Agent Taxonomy

| Class | Function | Typical Concurrency |
|---|---|---|
| **Crawler** | Fetches yard pages, respects robots.txt, rate-limits | 50–200 |
| **Extractor** | Parses HTML/JSON into raw part records | 100–400 |
| **Parser** | Domain-specific structural parsing (per yard schema) | 50–200 |
| **Normalizer** | Canonicalizes brands/models/categories/OEM refs | 20–80 |
| **Enricher** | Adds compatibility data, marketplace cross-refs | 10–40 |
| **Validator** | Schema validation, anomaly detection | 20–60 |
| **Deduper** | Clusters near-identical listings | 5–20 |

## Telemetry Envelope

```json
{
  "agent_id": "extractor-bparts-eu-07",
  "class": "extractor",
  "yard_id": "bparts-eu",
  "state": "running",
  "ts": "2026-05-20T14:32:11.482Z",
  "queue_depth": 142,
  "throughput_ppm": 38.4,
  "success_rate_60s": 0.978,
  "p95_latency_ms": 412,
  "tokens_used_1m": 18420,
  "tokens_budget_remaining": 0.62,
  "confidence_dist": {"<0.5": 4, "0.5-0.8": 22, ">0.8": 174},
  "last_error": null,
  "last_dedup_conflict": null
}
```

## UI Panels

- **Fleet grid**: cells = agent instances, color = state, size optionally scaled to throughput.
- **Per-agent dashboard**: 6-pane layout
  1. State timeline (last 1h)
  2. Throughput chart (parts/min)
  3. Latency p50/p95/p99
  4. Token usage burn-down
  5. Confidence histogram (rolling 5min)
  6. Error feed
- **Log stream**: SSE-backed `<LogViewer>`, supports filter by level/regex, autoscroll lock, pause-on-hover, copy-with-context.
- **Failure diagnostics modal**: stack trace, raw payload snippet (PII-redacted), suggested remediation, "open schema diff" link.
- **Confidence scoring panel**: per-class distribution; outlier alerts on confidence drift.
- **Duplicate detection telemetry**: dedup-cluster creation rate, conflict rate, manual-resolution backlog.

## Control Actions

| Action | Effect | Permission |
|---|---|---|
| Restart agent | Sends `restart` cmd via control bus | Operator+ |
| Drain queue | Stops new tasks, allows in-flight to complete | Operator+ |
| Adjust concurrency | Scales worker pool | Supervisor+ |
| Pause class | Stops all agents of a class | Supervisor+ |
| Emergency stop | Halts entire fleet | Admin only, double-confirm |

# SUPPLY VS DEMAND CORRELATION ENGINE

The Correlation Engine is the **analytical heart** of the platform — it transforms raw supply telemetry into actionable arbitrage signal.

## Signal Inputs

**Supply signals** (internal):
- New listing rate per category per region
- Price distribution per canonical part
- Freshness-weighted availability
- Yard reliability score

**Demand signals** (external, ingested by demand agents):
- eBay Motors Europe search velocity per OEM ref
- mobile.de parts search trends
- leboncoin / Allegro / AutoScout24 listing scarcity
- RockAuto out-of-stock pings
- Google Trends automotive part queries
- OEM dealer parts availability scrapes
- Manheim auction part demand

## Scoring Model (surfaced in UI)

```
opportunity_score = w1 * price_spread_normalized
                  + w2 * demand_velocity_score
                  + w3 * scarcity_signal
                  + w4 * supply_freshness
                  + w5 * confidence_aggregate
                  - p1 * logistics_friction
                  - p2 * decay_factor(time_since_signal)
```

Weights are operator-tunable per workspace in **Settings → Scoring Profiles**.

## UI Surfaces

- **Correlation matrix**: categorical heatmap (part category × demand region), cell click opens drilldown.
- **Opportunity feed**: ranked, infinite scroll, with explainability popover showing score breakdown.
- **Price-spread chart**: per opportunity, dual-axis showing supply price distribution vs demand market median.
- **Demand spike alerts**: WS-pushed cards when demand velocity > 2σ.
- **Scarcity signal indicators**: chips on parts where European stock < threshold.
- **Predictive opportunities**: ML-forecasted upcoming demand (seasonal: e.g., winter tires Sep–Oct, AC compressors May–Jun), shown in "Forecast" tab.
- **Recommendation layer**: each opportunity card carries `recommended_action`: BUY_NOW, MONITOR, BULK_ACQUIRE, IGNORE — with rationale.

## Decay & Freshness

Every opportunity carries a `decay_timer` rendered as a horizontal bar in the card. Half-life is category-dependent (electronics: 24h, body panels: 7d, engines: 14d). Opportunities are auto-archived past 3× half-life.

| Expanded | 12–16px | 56px | +1 step |

## Motion Philosophy

- **No decorative motion.** Animation exists only to convey state change.
- Duration tiers: 80ms (micro: hover, focus), 160ms (panels: collapse, expand), 240ms (modals, route transitions).
- Easing: `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` (standard) and `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` (emphasis).
- Reduced-motion: respects `prefers-reduced-motion`, disables all non-essential transitions.
- No parallax. No bounce. No page transitions beyond opacity crossfade.

# VISUAL LANGUAGE

The platform's visual identity is **industrial-tactical-instrumented**, drawing from:

- **Bloomberg Terminal**: monospace numeric density, amber-on-black headline data, brutal information hierarchy without ornament.
- **Palantir Gotham**: graph-driven investigative workflows, lineage trace breadcrumbs, surgical focus modes.
- **Automotive HMI** (Bosch DAS, fleet TMS, ECU diagnostics suites): industrial gauge aesthetics, blueprint-style line work, instrument-cluster spatial logic.

## Aesthetic Principles

1. **Black is the canvas.** The interface defaults to near-black (`#0A0D11`); panels are elevated by 1–2 luminance steps, never by drop shadows.
2. **Light is information.** Color is reserved for semantic state and data viz; chrome is monochrome.
3. **Numbers dominate.** Quantitative data is mono-spaced, right-aligned, and treated as primary content; labels are secondary.
4. **Borders, not shadows.** 1px borders in `--border-subtle` define structure; shadows used only on overlays.
5. **No gradients in chrome.** Gradients appear only in data visualizations (heat scales, sparklines fill).
6. **Iconography is utilitarian.** Line icons, 1.5px stroke, never illustrative.
7. **Avoid all startup tropes**: no glassmorphism, no neumorphism, no animated blobs, no marketing-style hero sections, no rounded-3xl cards, no pastel accent. The product looks like a tool, not a brand.

## Microcopy Tone

- Imperative, terse, technical. "Force re-crawl" not "Refresh the data".
- Numeric values shown raw with units (`38.4 ppm`, `412 ms`, `€12,840`, `0.978`).
- Timestamps in ISO 8601 in tables; relative in feeds ("2m ago").
- Error messages cite codes (`PARSE_ERR_217`) and link to runbook.

# UX PRINCIPLES

1. **Information-first, chrome-last.** Every pixel of chrome must justify itself against displaced data.
2. **Keyboard parity.** Every mouse action has a keyboard equivalent. Power users never touch the mouse.
3. **Deep-link everything.** Any view state must be expressible as a URL. Shareable, bookmarkable, reproducible.
4. **Auditability per row.** Every datum is traceable to its lineage in ≤2 clicks.
5. **Latency budgets are sacred.** No interaction may exceed 100ms perceived latency without explicit progress indication.
6. **State is reversible.** Every destructive or semi-destructive action is undoable for 10s via a toast.
7. **Confidence is always visible.** Never present derived data without surfacing its confidence.
8. **Density is a feature.** The default density assumes a senior operator on a large display. Comfortable mode is opt-out, not the baseline.
9. **Multi-operator awareness.** Presence indicators show who else is viewing or claiming an opportunity; conflicts are surfaced, not hidden.
10. **No surprise navigation.** Module switches preserve scroll, filters, and inspector state per module.

# DATA DENSITY STRATEGY

Density is engineered, not stumbled into. The platform commits to three operational density tiers and exposes a per-panel **density override** for power-user customization.

## Strategy Pillars

| Pillar | Implementation |
|---|---|
| **Hierarchical reveal** | Summary → row → expanded row → inspector → modal; each tier ~3-5× more detail |
| **Inline visualization** | Sparklines, micro-bars, heat strips inside table cells |
| **Progressive disclosure** | Advanced facets hidden behind "More" until pinned |
| **Aggregation pivots** | Toggle to group-by yard, brand, VIN, category at any time |
| **Compact numeric formats** | `€12.8k`, `1.2M rows`, `38.4ppm`, `p95 412ms` |
| **Sticky context** | Frozen columns, sticky headers, persistent filter bar |
| **Empty-state economy** | Empty panels collapse rather than reserving vertical space |

## Density Metrics (target)

| Surface | Target visible data points per 1080p viewport |
|---|---|
| Inventory Viewer (compact) | ≥ 40 rows × 14 columns = 560 cells |
| Agent Grid | ≥ 200 agent cells |
| Heatmap region inspector | ≥ 25 region rows |
| Opportunity Center | ≥ 18 cards |

## Cognitive Load Mitigation

- Maximum 7±2 simultaneous color encodings per view.
- Hover-only metadata for tertiary attributes; not rendered until requested.
- Configurable column sets saved as "views" per user.
- Smart defaults: most common filters pre-applied per role.

# PERFORMANCE ARCHITECTURE

## Target Metrics

| Metric | Target |
|---|---|
| First Contentful Paint (FCP) | < 1.2s on cold load (cable/wifi) |
| Time to Interactive (TTI) | < 2.5s |
| Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) | < 2.0s |
| Module route switch | < 300ms (cached), < 800ms (cold) |
| p95 interaction latency | < 100ms |
| WS message → UI reflect | < 50ms |
| Inventory table scroll | 60fps sustained on 1M rows |
| Memory ceiling (per tab) | < 600MB at 1M rows loaded |

## Tactics

### Row Virtualization
- `@tanstack/react-virtual` with measured row heights, `overscan: 10`.
- Columns virtualized horizontally when `columns.length > 20`.
- Row recycling via stable React keys (canonical part ID).

### Web Workers
- **Normalization worker**: bulk normalizes incoming WS deltas before merging into cache.
- **Dedup worker**: runs cluster similarity scoring client-side for selection-based dedup operations.
- **Search worker**: client-side fuzzy filter over loaded subset.
- Workers communicate via `comlink` for typed RPC.

### IndexedDB
- Local cache of: workspace prefs, saved queries, last-viewed inventory snapshot (capped at 50k rows for cold-start replay), normalized taxonomies (brands, models, categories).
- Powered by `idb` (Jake Archibald) with versioned schema migrations.
- Reconciled with server on app boot via ETag/If-None-Match.

### Code Splitting
- Per-module dynamic import; each PRIMARY MODULE = one chunk.
- Map (MapLibre GL ≈ 200KB gz) lazy-loaded only on Heatmap/Yard map routes.
- ECharts/visx lazy-loaded per chart type.
- Vendor chunk pinned across versions to maximize cache hit.

### Suspense Boundaries
- Module-level Suspense boundary with skeleton placeholder matching final layout (no CLS).
- Nested Suspense for inspector content so module shell remains interactive.
- Streaming SSR not used (auth-heavy app); CSR with prefetched data on hover for likely-next routes.

### Network
- HTTP/3 + Brotli static assets.
- API requests over HTTP/2 with `tanstack/query` deduplication and stale-while-revalidate.
- WS over WSS with `permessage-deflate` for payload compression.
- Critical CSS inlined; non-critical async.

### Memory
- Off-screen tabs throttle WS handlers (BroadcastChannel coordinates leader tab).
- Inventory cache evicts rows beyond viewport + buffer when memory > 400MB (heuristic).

# FRONT-END TECH STACK

| Layer | Choice | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| **Framework** | React 18+ | Concurrent rendering, Suspense, transitions critical for high-density UI under streaming load |
| **Language** | TypeScript 5+ (strict) | Non-negotiable for agent telemetry envelopes, query DSL, table column typing |
| **Build** | Vite 5+ | Sub-second HMR; Rollup-based production bundles; native ESM |
| **Routing** | TanStack Router | Type-safe routes, search-param state, loader pattern aligned with Query |
| **Server state** | TanStack Query v5 | Best-in-class cache, dedup, infinite queries, mutation rollback |
| **Client state** | Zustand + Immer | Minimal boilerplate, no provider hell, selectors prevent over-render. Redux Toolkit acceptable for very large teams; Zustand preferred for velocity. |
| **Tables** | TanStack Table v8 + `@tanstack/react-virtual` | Headless, virtualization-first, column pinning/grouping/resizing built-in |
| **Forms** | React Hook Form + Zod | Performant uncontrolled inputs, schema-first validation matching backend contracts |
| **Styling** | Tailwind CSS 4 + CVA | Atomic, design-token aware, variant-managed components |
| **Component primitives** | Radix UI | Unstyled, accessible, composable; pairs with Tailwind |
| **Maps** | MapLibre GL JS | Open-source, vector tiles, no Mapbox token tax; Mapbox GL acceptable if commercial style upgrades demanded |
| **Charts** | Apache ECharts (heavy/dense) + visx (custom/bespoke) | ECharts for production dashboards (5M+ point handling); visx for custom heatmaps, lineage graphs |
| **Graphs (DAG/lineage)** | React Flow + Cytoscape.js | React Flow for pipeline DAGs; Cytoscape for compatibility graphs |
| **Websockets** | Native `WebSocket` + custom client (with reconnection, backoff, multiplexing) | socket.io rejected — backend is bespoke; native WS minimizes overhead. Reconnect via exponential backoff capped at 30s. |
| **SSE** | Native `EventSource` for log streams | One-way streaming for logs; HTTP/2-friendly |
| **Worker bridge** | Comlink | Typed RPC over postMessage |
| **IDB wrapper** | `idb` | Minimal, promise-based |
| **DSL parsing** | Chevrotain | Performant LL(k) parser for query DSL |
| **Date/time** | `date-fns` + `date-fns-tz` | Tree-shakeable, locale-aware, TZ-explicit |
| **Internationalization** | Lingui or react-intl (deferred) | EN baseline; ES/DE/FR planned |
| **Testing** | Vitest + Testing Library + Playwright | Vitest for unit; Playwright for E2E + visual regression |
| **Storybook** | Storybook 8 | Component catalogue, density visual regression |
| **Linting** | ESLint + Biome (formatter) | Biome 10× faster than Prettier; ESLint for semantic rules |
| **Telemetry** | OpenTelemetry web SDK + custom instrumentation | Trace WS → cache → render paths; export to backend OTLP |
| **Error reporting** | Sentry (self-hosted) | Source-mapped, release-tagged |
| **Feature flags** | Self-hosted flagsmith or Unleash | Per-workspace toggles; off-network capable |

# STATE MANAGEMENT STRATEGY

The application enforces a **strict separation** between server-derived state (managed by TanStack Query) and ephemeral client UI state (managed by Zustand). This eliminates the most common source of bugs in real-time dashboards: dual sources of truth for the same datum.

## Layer Split

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  SERVER STATE — TanStack Query                               │
│  • Inventory pages, yards, agents, opportunities, metrics    │
│  • Cache key = canonical query descriptor                    │
│  • Mutations with optimistic updates + rollback              │
│  • Background refetch on focus, on reconnect, on WS hint     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  CLIENT UI STATE — Zustand (sliced)                          │
│  • workspaceStore: workspace, env, user prefs                │
│  • layoutStore: panel sizes, inspector pinned, density       │
│  • filterStore: per-module facet/filter state                │
│  • selectionStore: row selections, multi-select sets         │
│  • commandStore: command palette state                       │
│  • presenceStore: other operators, claims, locks             │
│  • wsStore: connection status, channel subscriptions         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  URL STATE — TanStack Router search params                   │
│  • Bookmarkable, shareable view state                        │
│  • Source of truth for module + filter + inspector entity    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Cache Invalidation Strategy

| Trigger | Invalidation |
|---|---|
| Mutation success | Targeted `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [...] })` |
| WS delta (`inventory.updated`) | `queryClient.setQueryData` for affected rows; invalidate facet counts |
| WS delta (`yard.status_changed`) | Patch yard query data; invalidate Scrap Yard list |
| WS delta (`agent.state`) | Patch agent query data; never invalidate (high frequency) |
| Window focus | Stale queries refetched if `staleTime` exceeded |
| Reconnection | Resubscribe channels; replay missed events via `since` cursor |

**Stale times** (tuned per data class):
- Inventory rows: 30s
- Yard list: 5min
- Agent telemetry: 5s
- Metrics: 10s
- Saved queries: 5min

## Optimistic Updates

Pattern for actions like "Mark as duplicate", "Claim opportunity":

```ts
useMutation({
  mutationFn: api.markDuplicate,
  onMutate: async (vars) => {
    await queryClient.cancelQueries({ queryKey: ['inventory', vars.id] });
    const prev = queryClient.getQueryData(['inventory', vars.id]);
    queryClient.setQueryData(['inventory', vars.id], (old) => ({ ...old, _dedup_status: 'pending' }));
    return { prev };
  },
  onError: (_err, vars, ctx) => {
    queryClient.setQueryData(['inventory', vars.id], ctx?.prev);
    toast.error('Mark-duplicate failed. Reverted.');
  },
  onSettled: (_data, _err, vars) => {
    queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['inventory', vars.id] });
  },
});
```

## WebSocket → Cache Reconciliation

A central `useWebSocketReconciler` hook subscribes to channels and dispatches typed handlers:

```ts
on('inventory.delta', (msg) => {
  msg.upserts.forEach(row => {
    queryClient.setQueryData(['inventory', row.id], (old) => ({ ...old, ...row }));
  });
  msg.deletes.forEach(id => {
    queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: ['inventory', id] });
  });
  // Bump list queries to indicate staleness
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['inventory', 'list'], refetchType: 'none' });
});
```

`refetchType: 'none'` marks lists stale without forcing refetch; user-visible lists refetch on next viewport scroll trigger.

# REAL-TIME SYNCHRONIZATION MODEL

## Channels

| Channel | Cardinality | Payload | Cadence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `events:global` | Singleton | KPI deltas, alerts | 1–5/s |
| `events:agent-state` | Per-agent or aggregated | Telemetry envelopes | 10–100/s aggregated |
| `events:inventory-delta` | Sharded by region | Upserts/deletes | Bursty, 1–500/s |
| `events:yard-sync` | Per-yard | Sync start/complete/error | 0.1–1/s |
| `events:opportunity-new` | Singleton | New ranked opportunities | 0.01–1/s |
| `events:schema-drift` | Singleton | Yard schema change alerts | Rare, critical |
| `events:presence` | Per-workspace | Operator presence/claims | 0.1–1/s |
| `logs:agent:{id}` | Per-agent (SSE) | Raw log lines | 1–50/s per agent |
| `pipeline:run:{id}` | Per-run | Pipeline state transitions | 0.1–1/s |

## Message Envelope

```ts
interface WSMessage<T = unknown> {
  v: 1;                    // protocol version
  id: string;              // ULID, idempotency key
  ts: string;              // ISO 8601, ms precision
  channel: string;         // e.g. "events:inventory-delta"
  type: string;            // e.g. "inventory.upsert"
  seq: number;             // monotonic per channel
  payload: T;
  causation_id?: string;   // optional, links to triggering event
  agent_id?: string;       // optional, source agent
}
```

The client maintains a per-channel `lastSeq` cursor. On reconnect, it sends `subscribe` with `since: lastSeq`; the server replays missed messages.

## Connection Lifecycle

```
[CONNECT] → [AUTH] → [SUBSCRIBE *] → [STREAMING] ─ heartbeat ──┐
                                          │                      │
                                  [HEARTBEAT_LOSS]               │
                                          ↓                      │
                                    [RECONNECT]                  │
                                          ↓                      │
                              [BACKOFF: 0.5s,1s,2s,5s,10s,30s]   │
                                          ↓                      │
                                    [RESUBSCRIBE w/ since]       │
                                          └──────────────────────┘
```

- Heartbeat: client → server ping every 25s; server → client pong; missed pong twice → reconnect.
- Backoff: exponential with jitter, capped at 30s.
- Auth: short-lived JWT in initial subscribe frame; refresh via `/api/auth/refresh` before expiry.

## Idempotency

Every WS message carries a ULID `id`. The client maintains a 5-minute LRU of seen IDs; duplicates are dropped silently. Mutations carry client-generated idempotency keys propagated to the server.

## Multi-Tab Coordination

- A `BroadcastChannel('apax-intel')` elects a **leader tab** via Web Locks API.
- Only the leader maintains the WS connection; followers receive events via BroadcastChannel.
- On leader tab close, follower auto-promotes (< 200ms).
- Mutations from any tab are proxied to leader, executed, and broadcast back.

## Presence

The presence subsystem publishes:

```ts
{
  user_id: string;
  workspace: string;
  module: string;
  view_state: { entityId?: string; filterHash?: string };
  claimed_entities: string[];   // e.g. opportunity IDs being worked
  ts: string;
}
```

Rendered as `<PresenceAvatars>` in module headers and as inline locks on claimed cards.

# OPERATIONAL WORKFLOWS

## Workflow 1: New Yard Onboarding
1. OSINT analyst submits yard candidate via "Add yard" CTA in Scrap Yard Explorer.
2. System schedules a discovery crawl; `crawler-discovery` agent inspects robots.txt, sitemap, schema fingerprint.
3. Schema fingerprint compared to known templates; if novel, queued for `parser` agent template authoring.
4. Once parser template merged, yard enters `pilot` status: limited crawl, manual review of first 500 extractions.
5. Analyst confirms quality in Inventory Viewer (filtered by yard); status promoted to `active`.
6. Yard appears in default views; agents auto-scaled per yard volume.

## Workflow 2: Arbitrage Opportunity Lifecycle
1. Correlation engine emits `opportunity.new` via WS.
2. Opportunity Center surfaces card; sound alert if score > 0.9.
3. Strategist reviews card detail; inspects supply lineage and demand evidence.
4. Strategist clicks **Claim** → presence lock broadcast to other operators.
5. Push-to-ERP optionally triggers procurement; status transitions `claimed → procured`.
6. Outbound listing created in marketplace via Export & Pipeline Console.
7. On sale, sale event ingested; opportunity marked `realized`; P&L sparkline updates.

## Workflow 3: Schema Drift Resolution
1. `crawler` agent detects DOM signature mismatch; emits `schema.drift` event.
2. Scraping Health Monitor surfaces drift alert.
3. Platform engineer opens schema diff viewer; reviews structural changes.
4. Engineer updates parser template; deploys via CI.
5. Affected yard re-enters pilot status for 24h; extractions monitored.
6. On confirmation, yard returns to `active`; alert auto-resolves.

## Workflow 4: Duplicate Resolution
1. Deduper agent emits `dedup.cluster.uncertain` (similarity 0.7–0.9, needs human).
2. Cluster appears in Duplicate Detection Panel conflict queue.
3. Inventory engineer opens cluster detail; reviews side-by-side image grid + attribute diff.
4. Engineer confirms cluster (merge), splits a member, or promotes a different canonical.
5. Decision fed back as training signal to dedup model.

## Workflow 5: Agent Failure Triage
1. Agent enters `erroring` state; alert published to Global Dashboard.
2. AI Supervisor clicks alert → deep-link to Agent Activity Monitor with agent selected.
3. Failure diagnostics panel shows last 100 errors, payload snippet, suggested runbook.
4. Supervisor restarts agent or escalates to platform engineer.
5. Restart event audited; resolution time tracked in error budget burndown.

## Workflow 6: Cross-Module Investigation
1. Analyst sees demand spike for "BMW E46 M54 engine" in Correlation matrix.
2. Click cell → drill to opportunities filtered by category × region.
3. From an opportunity, click "Investigate signal" → Parts Intelligence Panel for canonical part.
4. From Parts Intel, click yard chip → Scrap Yard Explorer pre-filtered.
5. From yard, click "Open inventory →" → Inventory Viewer with yard + category pre-applied.
6. Throughout, breadcrumb trail preserved in URL; investigation shareable.

# SCALABILITY CONSIDERATIONS

## Multi-Monitor Support
- Layout is built on CSS Grid with named regions; each region can be **popped out** into a new browser window via the Window Management API (`window.open` + state sync via BroadcastChannel).
- Operator can run Global Dashboard on monitor 1, Inventory Viewer on monitor 2, Agent Monitor on monitor 3.
- Detached windows share WS connection via leader-elected tab; selections and presence sync across windows.

## 4K and Ultrawide Layouts
- Breakpoints: 1366, 1680, 1920, 2560, 3440 (ultrawide), 3840 (4K).
- At 2560+, three-column module layouts unlock (e.g., Inventory: facets | table | inspector).
- At 4K, density mode defaults to `compact`; font scaling honors `--root-font-size` workspace pref.
- Map and chart canvases use `devicePixelRatio`-aware rendering for sharp HiDPI output.

## Keyboard-First Navigation
- Global focus management via roving tabindex within tables and grids.
- Module hotkeys: `g d` → Global Dashboard, `g y` → Scrap Yard, `g i` → Inventory, `g a` → Agents, `g o` → Opportunities, `g h` → Heatmap.
- Inventory table: `j/k` row nav, `enter` open inspector, `x` toggle select, `/` focus query, `f` open facet sidebar, `e` export selection.
- Command palette: `Cmd+K` always, fuzzy across actions + entities + saved queries.

## Command Palette
- Three result classes: **Actions** (run command), **Navigation** (jump to entity), **Recent** (recent items).
- Indexed via Fuse.js with weighted fields.
- Inline parameters: `claim opportunity 4821`, `export inventory bmw e46 csv`.

## Shortcut Grid (`Cmd+/` opens reference)

| Scope | Key | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Global | `Cmd+K` | Command palette |
| Global | `Cmd+/` | Shortcut reference |
| Global | `Cmd+Shift+D` | Cycle density |
| Global | `Cmd+B` | Toggle left rail |
| Global | `Cmd+J` | Toggle inspector |
| Global | `g g` | Global Dashboard |
| Global | `g y` | Yard Explorer |
| Global | `g i` | Inventory |
| Global | `g a` | Agents |
| Global | `g o` | Opportunities |
| Global | `g h` | Heatmap |
| Table | `j` / `k` | Row down / up |
| Table | `gg` / `G` | First / last row |
| Table | `Enter` | Open inspector |
| Table | `x` | Toggle row selection |
| Table | `Shift+x` | Range-select |
| Table | `e` | Export selection |
| Table | `f` | Toggle facet sidebar |
| Table | `/` | Focus query bar |
| Inspector | `Esc` | Close |
| Inspector | `p` | Pin |
| Inspector | `[` / `]` | Prev / next entity |

## Horizontal Scale
- The front-end is stateless beyond browser caches; multiple operators scale linearly.
- API layer expected to scale via read replicas + read-through caching (Redis); WS via Redis pub/sub fan-out.
- For workspaces exceeding 5M SKUs, server-side filtering is mandatory; client-side facet computation disabled with banner notice.

# FINAL RECOMMENDATIONS

1. **Treat the Inventory Visualization Engine as a tier-zero subsystem.** Resource it as a dedicated team. Build a benchmarking harness early (10k, 100k, 1M rows) and gate releases on regression. The IVE is the single point of failure for operator productivity.

2. **Build the design system before the screens.** Ship Storybook with all primitives, compounds, and density variants prior to module implementation. Every module screen should be assembled from pre-existing, pre-reviewed components. No bespoke styling in screen files.

3. **Invest in the WS infrastructure early.** The reconciler hook, idempotency layer, leader-tab election, and channel multiplexing are foundational. Cutting corners here causes ghost updates, stale cache, and operator distrust — which is fatal in an intelligence tool.

4. **Make telemetry first-class.** Instrument every interaction, every WS message, every cache hit/miss. Ship a developer-facing diagnostics panel (toggle with `Cmd+Shift+I`) showing cache state, WS lag, render counts. This pays for itself within weeks.

5. **Adopt aggressive code splitting from day one.** Each PRIMARY MODULE is a chunk. Map, charts, graph libraries lazy-loaded. The first paint must be < 1.2s even on slow connections to avoid eroding operator trust on cold loads.

6. **Defer i18n but plan for it.** Use ICU message format placeholders from day one even with EN-only strings. Adding ES/DE/FR later becomes a translation task rather than a refactor.

7. **Resist the temptation to soften the UI.** Pressure will come to add rounded corners, gradients, friendlier copy, illustrative icons. Reject it. The aesthetic is the product's authority signal — operators trust the tool because it looks like one.

8. **Build the command palette first, not last.** Once it ships, every new feature becomes a one-line registration. It is the highest-leverage UI pattern in dense applications.

9. **Treat audit trails as features, not compliance.** Every action button should write an audit row. The lineage trace is a competitive moat: no startup competitor will invest in it, and enterprise operators consider it table stakes.

10. **Reserve a "tactical" mode.** Implement a fullscreen, chrome-less, monitor-grade layout (think NORAD wall display) for war-room scenarios — flash sales, peak demand events, system-wide incidents. It is rarely used but disproportionately memorable when it is.

11. **Plan for the agent feedback loop.** Today's UI surfaces agent telemetry; tomorrow's UI must let supervisors **adjust agent behavior** (concurrency, confidence thresholds, scoring weights) inline. Architect the state layer to support write-back to agent configs early.

12. **Hold the line on density.** Every product matures toward sparser UI under user-research pressure. Resist. The operators you are building for prefer 60 rows on screen over 12. The wrong audience will complain; ignore them — they are not the buyer.

### **You** `01:06`

python-jose que es eso?

### **Claude** `01:07`

`python-jose` es una librería Python que implementa el estándar **JOSE** (JavaScript Object Signing and Encryption) — el conjunto de specs de IETF para firmar y cifrar tokens y mensajes JSON. En la práctica se usa sobre todo para:

- **JWT** (JSON Web Tokens) — los tokens firmados que se usan en sistemas de autenticación (login, sesiones, OAuth2).
- **JWS** (JSON Web Signatures) — firma criptográfica de payloads.
- **JWE** (JSON Web Encryption) — cifrado de payloads.
- **JWK** (JSON Web Keys) — formato de representación de claves.

Es básicamente la implementación Python "todo en uno" para trabajar con tokens criptográficos JSON. Suele aparecer en plantillas FastAPI de autenticación (de hecho, la documentación oficial de FastAPI la usa en su tutorial de OAuth2).

**Por qué estaba en nuestro `requirements.txt`**: lo más probable es que viniera de un scaffold inicial del backend (cuando se montó FastAPI) "por si se implementaba auth con JWT". Nunca llegó a usarse — `grep` en `backend/*.py` confirmó 0 importaciones de `jose`, `jwt`, ni `ecdsa`.

**Si en el futuro necesitamos JWT**: hoy lo más recomendado es **PyJWT** directamente (más mantenido, menos superficie de ataque) o **authlib**. `python-jose` arrastra `ecdsa` y `rsa` aunque solo uses HMAC, que es justamente lo que te hace pagar CVEs de algoritmos que no usas — exactamente lo que nos pasó.

Audit completo. Resumen estructural:

## Lo que hace `bridge-aurelius.py`

1. **Lee** `sessions/session-YYYY-MM-DD.md` (formato markdown con `### **You**` / `### **Claude**`)
2. **Genera diálogo** con **Gemini 2.5-flash** (NO Ollama — usa API key `GEMINI_API_KEY`)
3. **Renderiza** HTML del episodio (con clases `avatar-claude`, `speaker-aurelius`, etc.)
4. **Inyecta** en `lyai.online/index.html` reemplazando el bloque `<!-- Next episode -->`
5. **Git commit + push** automático

## Rutas hardcoded incompatibles con server

```python
PROJECT_DIR  = Path(__file__).parent                        # ahora = /opt/lyai/app/lyai.online/
SESSIONS_DIR = PROJECT_DIR / "sessions"                     # ❌ no existe en server
LYAI_ONLINE  = PROJECT_DIR / "lyai.online" / "index.html"   # ❌ ruta anidada absurda en server
```

En tu WSL el layout es `~/projects/{bridge-aurelius.py, sessions/, lyai.online/index.html}`. En server tendría que ser `{bridge-aurelius.py, sessions/<algo>, /var/www/lyai.online/index.html}`.

## Otras dependencias WSL

| Pieza | ¿Dónde está? | ¿Necesaria? |
|---|---|---|
| `archive-session.py` | Solo WSL | ✅ Sí — produce el `session-YYYY-MM-DD.md` que bridge consume |
| `sessions/session-YYYY-MM-DD.md` | Solo WSL | ✅ Sí — input de bridge |
| `update-state.sh` | Solo WSL | ⚠ Posible — orquestador diario |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` env var | WSL `.env` | ✅ Sí — Gemini 2.5-flash (free tier) |

## Dos caminos a elegir

**Camino 1 · Port directo (rápido · más fideilidad)**:
- Copia desde WSL: `scp ~/projects/archive-session.py ~/projects/update-state.sh ~/projects/sessions lyai@178.63.165.87:/opt/lyai/app/lyai.online/`
- Adapto paths en bridge-aurelius.py (3 constantes)
- Pongo `GEMINI_API_KEY` en `/opt/lyai/app/lyai.online/.env`
- Cron en server: `0 4 * * * cd /opt/lyai/app/lyai.online && python3 update-state.sh` (o equivalente)
- ✅ Mismo formato exacto. Cero riesgo de regression visual.

**Camino 2 · Rewrite usando JSONL del server (más limpio · más trabajo)**:
- Adapto `extract_context()` para leer JSONL desde `/home/lyai/.claude/projects/**.jsonl` directamente
- Salto el paso `archive-session.py` (no hace falta el `.md` intermedio)
- Sin dependencia de `update-state.sh`
- ⚠ Coste: ~1-2h de rewrite + test. Puede haber drift en formato/calidad.

Sugiero **Camino 1** primero porque te da autonomía YA — luego en otra sesión se puede limpiar a Camino 2. ¿`procede`?

## Lo que `archive-session.py` necesita adaptar

## Lo que `update-state.sh` hace (no aplicable al server)

Es un orchestrador grande con tareas WSL-only (ssh-to-server, deploy desde WSL, wiki sync desde prod, etc.). En el server no tiene sentido portarlo entero — la mitad sería ssh-to-self.

## Pipeline mínimo necesario en server

Solo 2 pasos del flujo completo:
1. `archive-session.py --date YYYY-MM-DD` → genera `sessions/session-YYYY-MM-DD.md` desde JSONL del día
2. `bridge-aurelius.py --date YYYY-MM-DD` → genera episodio + inyecta en `/var/www/lyai.online/index.html`

## Propuesta (no aplico todavía)

**Paso A · Adaptar archive-session.py para server**:
```diff
- JSONL_DIR = Path.home() / ".claude/projects/-home-aipa-projects"
+ JSONL_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("JSONL_DIR", Path.home() / ".claude/projects"))
```
Y cambiar `find_all_jsonl()` para usar `rglob("*.jsonl")` (recursive, captura todos los subdirs por proyecto).

**Paso B · Escribir `generate-daily-episode.sh` minimal** (NO portar update-state.sh):
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Pipeline diario · archive + episode + deploy
cd /opt/lyai/app/lyai.online
TODAY=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)
python3 archive-session.py --date "$TODAY" --no-git
python3 bridge-aurelius.py --date "$TODAY" --no-git
```

**Paso C · Dry-run con 2026-05-03** (la primera fecha sin episodio · ahí está "Episode 050 placeholder"):
```bash
python3 archive-session.py --date 2026-05-03 --force --no-git
python3 bridge-aurelius.py --date 2026-05-03 --dry-run --no-git
```

Si dry-run sale bien, hago el run sin `--dry-run`. Si el episodio queda OK visualmente, hacemos backfill para 2026-05-04, 05, 06, 10, 11...20.

**Paso D · Cron** (después de backfill exitoso):
```cron
# /etc/cron.d/lyai-online-mirror-protocol
0 4 * * * lyai cd /opt/lyai/app/lyai.online && ./generate-daily-episode.sh >> /var/log/lyai-online.log 2>&1
```

¿`procede` con Paso A + Paso B + Paso C (dry-run)? Si dry-run sale OK te enseño el output antes de inyectar.

### **Claude** `04:52`

El feed es lo que renderiza `renderEvents()` en [services.tsx:2645+](frontend/app/services.tsx#L2645). Estructura:

```
┌─ Tabs ─────────────────────────────┐
│  [Local · station]  [Tout PdS · N] │  ← evtTab: 'local' / 'pds'
└────────────────────────────────────┘

  Inspirations · Portes du Soleil    ← carrusel auto-scroll
  [Freeride] [Champéry] [Rock the Pistes] [Rando Parc]...

  ── Events list ──
  Si displayEvents.length === 0:
    "Aucun événement cette semaine" + ícono calendar  ← empty state
  Si hay eventos:
    Lista de cards con icon por tipo (music/food/sport/party/promotion/other)
```

Fuentes de datos:
- `eventsData` (tab Local) — eventos de la station seleccionada
- `globalEventsData` (tab Tout PdS) — eventos de las 12 estaciones

## Por qué te preguntas si existe

Sospecho que has llegado a la sub-sección "Événements" y has visto **solo el carrusel de inspirations + el empty state** ("Aucun événement cette semaine"). Eso **es** el feed — pero hoy probablemente está vacío de eventos reales porque:

1. El post "Restaurant démo · hotel chez jan completo toda la semana" del home es un **LBL update** (owner_updates), NO un evento. Vive en `liveUpdates` no en `eventsData`.
2. Para que aparezca en el feed de Événements debe estar publicado con **cross-post como evento** (el switch que vimos hace días en el OwnerConsole: "conserje+événements")

¿Quieres que confirme con curl qué hay en cada endpoint?
- `GET /api/owner-updates` → lo que ves en home (LBL)
- `GET /api/events?station=<id>&scope=local` → lo que renderEvents() pinta

O directamente: ¿qué prefieres que muestre el card del home — el feed LBL (donde está el post) o el feed Événements (donde estaría si fuera cross-post)?

### **Claude** `05:10`

Aquí está el detalle: hay **2 fuentes de datos separadas**.

| Lo que ves | Endpoint | Datos |
|---|---|---|
| Card "Dernière heure" en home | `/api/business/updates` | LBL owner_updates · **2+ posts activos** (incluyendo "Hôtel complet toute la semaine" de Chez Jan) |
| "ÉVÉNEMENTS · DÉTAIL" en /lbl | `/api/events` | events table · **0 entries** |

## Por qué la discrepancia

Cuando publicas algo desde el OwnerConsole hay un switch `publishTo`:
- `chat_only` → escribe solo en `lyai.owner_updates` (aparece en home + LBL OWNERS · NO en events)
- `event_and_chat` → escribe en **ambas** tablas (aparece en todos sitios)

El post de Chez Jan fue publicado como `chat_only` (default actual del OwnerConsole · [lbl.tsx:699](frontend/app/lbl.tsx#L699): `useState<...>('chat_only')`). Por eso aparece en home pero no en events.

## Opciones de fix

| Opción | Cambio | Pros / Contras |
|---|---|---|
| **A** · Cambiar default a `event_and_chat` | 1 línea en `lbl.tsx` | Todo se cross-postea por defecto · más visible · puede generar ruido si post no es "evento" |
| **B** · Detección automática del tipo | LLM extractor decide `chat_only` vs `event_and_chat` según contenido | Lo correcto · pero requiere más lógica |
| **C** · Fusionar events feed para INCLUIR owner_updates con duración multi-día | Backend: `/api/events` añade owner_updates con `duration_kind='multi_day'` o `'indefinite'` | Sin tocar publish UX · "completo toda la semana" cualifica como evento de facto |
| **D** · Aceptar separación · entrenar al user a marcar el switch | Cero código | Mantiene pureza de datos pero requiere disciplina del owner |

**Recomendación**: **C** porque casa con la intuición del usuario — un post que dura una semana es de hecho un "evento" desde el punto de vista del consumidor. Mantiene los datos separados a nivel BD pero unifica en el feed visible. ~20 líneas backend.

¿Cuál?

|---|---|---|

## Por qué NO se hace automático

**Respuesta técnica**: en Claude Code la única manera de ejecutar algo "siempre que pase X" es vía **hooks configurados en `~/.claude/settings.json`**. Los hooks son comandos shell que el harness dispara en eventos concretos.

Eventos disponibles relevantes:
- `Stop` — cuando Claude termina de generar respuesta
- `UserPromptSubmit` — cuando user envía mensaje (se puede escanear keywords)
- `SessionStart` — cuando arranca la sesión

**Lo que hay hoy**: no hay hook configurado para detectar "cerrar conversación / nueva ventana". Por eso solo yo, si recuerdo el protocolo, lo invoco.

**Memorias/preferencias markdown NO pueden** forzar comportamientos automáticos · solo informan a Claude cuando se cargan al inicio · requieren que YO active el protocolo voluntariamente · y por eso "se me escapa".

### Solución concreta

Configurar uno de estos:

| Opción | Funciona | Coste |
|---|---|---|
| **Hook `UserPromptSubmit`** que escanee keywords ("terminar conversación", "nueva ventana", "cerrar sesión") y dispare `save-session` o un script de cierre | Sí · funciona inmediatamente | Editar `settings.json` con un matcher + bash script (~15 min) |
| **Hook `Stop`** que después de cada respuesta verifique si el user dijo algo de cierre y si sí, prompt al usuario | Sí | Más complejo (mantener estado) |
| **Slash command `/end-session`** que el user invoca al cerrar | Sí · pero requiere que el user se acuerde | Trivial (1 markdown file en `commands/`) |
| **Skill `save-session`** auto-invocada por mi instrucción "siempre al detectar keyword X" | ❌ NO funciona · memorias no fuerzan comportamiento | — |

Recomiendo **Hook `UserPromptSubmit`** con un script bash que:
1. Detecta keywords de cierre en el mensaje
2. Si match → injecta system reminder a Claude del tipo "el user va a cerrar · ejecuta protocolo save-session"
3. Claude lo ve y lo ejecuta

¿Quieres que (1) primero termine el cierre manual de esta sesión (creo las 4 entradas memoria/wiki + SESSION_LOG), y luego (2) propongamos el hook `UserPromptSubmit` para que la próxima vez sea automático?

## Propuesta · 2 archivos (no aplico todavía)

### 1. Script bash · `/opt/lyai/wiki/tools/detect_session_close_intent.sh`

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Hook UserPromptSubmit · detecta intención de cierre y inyecta system-reminder
# con el checklist del PROTOCOLO-CIERRE-AURELIO.md (Capa Agente).

PROMPT=$(cat)

if echo "$PROMPT" | grep -iqE "(cerrar (esta )?(conversaci[oó]n|sesi[oó]n|ventana)|nueva ventana|dar por terminada|terminar (esta )?sesi[oó]n|abrir(é| una) nueva|end (this )?session)"; then
  cat <<'EOF'
<system-reminder>
Detectada intención de CIERRE de sesión. ANTES de cerrar ejecuta el PROTOCOLO-CIERRE-AURELIO.md (Capa Agente):

1. INDEX.md · añadir cierres de flags AUR/OPS/SEC tocadas (skip si ninguna)
   Path: /opt/lyai/audits/INDEX.md

2. Audit consolidado · cierres + propuestas pendientes + bloqueos user
   Path: /opt/lyai/audits/YYYY-MM-DD-{agent-id}-{session-slug}/README.md

3. Memoria persistente · feedback_*/project_*/reference_*.md por lección NO obvia
   Path: ~/.claude/projects/-{proyecto}/memory/ + update MEMORY.md
   Buscar memorias existentes ANTES de crear (no duplicar)

4. Channel Aurelius · mensaje msg_type:"session_close" con marker AUR-065
   Path: /opt/lyai/app/channels/Aurelius.jsonl
   AUR-065 obligatorio: context=(server|WSL builder|...) + verificable (SHA/comando/SELECT)

Protocolo completo: /home/lyai/.claude/PROTOCOLO-CIERRE-AURELIO.md
Capa Técnica (update-state.sh) solo aplica al WSL builder, NO a server/web.
</system-reminder>
EOF
fi
exit 0
```

### 2. Edit a `~/.claude/settings.json` · añadir bajo `hooks`:

```json
"UserPromptSubmit": [
  {
    "matcher": "",
    "hooks": [
      {
        "type": "command",
        "command": "/opt/lyai/wiki/tools/detect_session_close_intent.sh",
        "timeout": 5
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

## Cómo funciona

1. User envía mensaje (cualquier mensaje)
2. Harness ejecuta el script · le pasa el prompt por stdin
3. Si el regex matchea keywords de cierre → script imprime `<system-reminder>` con el checklist completo
4. Harness inyecta esa salida en mi context window
5. Yo lo leo y ejecuto el protocolo voluntariamente

**Cobertura del regex**: "cerrar conversación", "cerrar sesión", "cerrar ventana", "nueva ventana", "dar por terminada", "terminar sesión", "abriré una nueva", "abrir una nueva", "end session", "end this session" (case-insensitive).

**Riesgo**: 0. Si no matchea → script termina sin output → comportamiento idéntico al actual. Es puramente aditivo.

¿`aplica`? Si dices sí, creo el script (chmod +x) y edito settings.json en una sola pasada · luego haces test (en mensaje próximo escribiendo "voy a cerrar la conversación") · debería verme inyectar el reminder antes de responder.

## Alternativas si Obsidian no usa `~/projects/wiki/`

Pregúntame qué path tiene tu vault Obsidian configurado y te doy el comando exacto. Tres patrones comunes:

| Vault path probable | Cómo refrescar |
|---|---|
| `~/projects/wiki/` (la convención que veo en tu repo) | `cd ~/projects/wiki && git pull` |
| `~/Documents/Obsidian/LyAi/` o similar (si tienes vault separado · symlink al repo) | `cd /path/al/vault && git pull` |

Si tu vault es el clone git directo, después del pull Obsidian detecta los archivos nuevos automáticamente (puede que tengas que recargar con Cmd/Ctrl+R) y los podrás navegar con los `[[wikilinks]]` que dejé en los `.md` (ej. `[[reference-hetzner-ipv6-broken-googleapis]]`).

### **Claude** `07:08`

Error de Obsidian intentando hacer `watch` sobre un directorio · pasa a menudo cuando vault está en filesystem WSL accedido vía Windows UNC `\\wsl.localhost\...`. El protocolo 9P entre Windows ↔ WSL2 no soporta inotify de manera fiable y Obsidian Electron (file watcher Chokidar) se atraganta.

**No es algo del lado server** · es entorno Windows/WSL en tu máquina.

## Soluciones (de menos a más invasiva)

### A · Recargar app (rápido · prueba primero)

Botón "Recargar la aplicación" en el error. A veces el watcher fallaba en arranque y al reintento funciona.

### B · Borrar workspace cache de Obsidian del vault

```bash
# Desde WSL terminal:
rm /home/aipa/projects/wiki/LyAi\ -\ Vault/.obsidian/workspace.json 2>/dev/null
rm /home/aipa/projects/wiki/LyAi\ -\ Vault/.obsidian/workspace-mobile.json 2>/dev/null
```

Luego abrir vault otra vez · Obsidian regenera el workspace.

### C · Mover el vault a Windows nativo (solución definitiva)

WSL2 + Obsidian Windows = problemas crónicos con file watching. Patrón recomendado:

1. En Windows nativo (no WSL), clonar el repo:
   ```powershell
   cd C:\Users\<tu_usuario>\Documents\
   git clone git@github.com:LyAi-labs/lyai-wiki.git Obsidian-LyAi-Wiki
   ```
2. Abrir esa carpeta como vault desde Obsidian (sin `\\wsl.localhost\`)
3. Para sincronizar: `git pull` periódico (manual o vía Obsidian Git plugin)
4. WSL sigue siendo donde trabajas con scripts · Windows es solo viewer Obsidian

Con esto el watch usa NTFS nativo · sin bug.

### D · Plugin Obsidian Git para no depender de file watching

Si quieres seguir con vault en WSL: instala plugin **Obsidian Git** y configúralo para auto-pull cada X minutos. El plugin no depende de file watch del SO · usa polling git interno. Workaround si Obsidian se sigue rompiendo con A+B.

## 2 · Abrir como vault en Obsidian

1. En Obsidian: selector de bóvedas → **"Abrir otra bóveda"**
2. **"Abrir carpeta como bóveda"** → navega a `C:\Users\Glado\Documents\GitHub\lyai-wiki\` (la carpeta del repo · NO una subcarpeta)

1. Obsidian → **Settings (⚙️)** → **Community plugins** → "Turn on community plugins"

## 4 · Configurar auto-pull

En Settings → Community plugins → Obsidian Git → **Options**:

| Setting | Valor recomendado |
|---|---|
| **Vault backup interval (minutes)** | `0` (NO auto-commit · solo queremos pull) |
| **Pull updates on startup** | ✓ ON (cada vez que abras Obsidian se sincroniza) |
| **Auto pull interval (minutes)** | `10` (revisa cambios cada 10 min mientras tienes Obsidian abierto) |
| **Auto pull on startup** | ✓ ON |
| **Disable notifications** | OFF (que te avise cuando hay cambios) |

Si la primera vez te pide credenciales: usa tu GitHub username + PAT (lo crearás 1 vez y queda guardado). Si usaste GitHub Desktop antes, debería usar las credenciales del manager y no preguntarte.

- Si pulled: aparecerán mis 6 archivos en sidebar izquierdo

A partir de aquí · cada vez que algún Claude (server) añada algo al wiki, en 10 min lo tienes en Obsidian sin tocar nada.

## Configuración

Click **"Opciones"** (el primer botón) y rellena:

| Setting | Valor |
|---|---|
| **Commit-and-sync interval (minutes)** | `0` |
| **Auto pull interval (minutes)** | `10` |
| **Pull updates on startup** | ✓ ON |
| **Auto pull on startup** | ✓ ON (si existe esa opción separada) |
| **Disable notifications** | OFF (déjalo desactivado para ver confirmaciones) |

El resto déjalo por defecto.

## Test inmediato

**Ctrl+P** → busca `Git: Pull` → ejecutar.

Resultados esperados:
- **"Already up to date"** · si ya tienes los últimos commits → todo bien
- **"Pulled N changes"** · si había deltas → bien también, ya están en tu vault
- **Pide credenciales** · necesitas Personal Access Token (te explico abajo)

## Si pide credenciales (PAT)

GitHub Desktop guardó creds en su propio manager, pero el plugin Git usa libgit2 independiente · puede que pida la primera vez:

1. https://github.com/settings/tokens
2. **Generate new token (classic)** → nombre: `obsidian-git-plugin` → scope: **solo `repo`** → 90 días (o no-expire si confías)
3. **Generate token** → cópialo (lo verás 1 sola vez)
4. Pega como password cuando el plugin pregunte (username = tu GitHub username)

Windows guarda esa credencial · no te la vuelve a pedir.

## Verificación final

Cuando puedas ejecutar `Git: Pull` sin error · ya está. Cada 10 min Obsidian comprueba GitHub. Próxima vez que añada algo al wiki desde el server, llega solo.

## Sobre "cerrar sesión"

Cerré el **protocolo** (memorias, wiki, channel, audit, etc.) · pero la ventana de conversación sigue abierta · si quieres cerrar físicamente cierras el tab/ventana en Claude Code. Yo no controlo eso.

## Plugins para mejorar el graph view

Sí · hay varios. Los más usados:

| Plugin | Qué hace | Coste cognitivo |
|---|---|---|
| **Extended Graph** | Más customización del graph nativo: colores por carpeta, tags como nodos, tamaño de nodo por # links, etiquetas legibles a más zoom out | Bajo · solo añade opciones · sigue siendo el graph de Obsidian |
| **Juggl** | Implementación alternativa basada en Cytoscape.js · layouts radicalmente distintos (hierárquico, circular, dagre, etc.) · estética muy editorial | Medio · es OTRO graph paralelo · curva de aprendizaje |
| **3D Graph** | Mismo graph pero en 3D · navegable con mouse · espectacular pero menos práctico | Bajo · solo wow factor |
| **Graph Analysis** | Calcula métricas (centralidad, comunidades, PageRank) y resalta nodos importantes | Bajo · útil si quieres saber qué notas son "hubs" |
| **Graph Banner** | Embed un sub-graph como banner dentro de cada nota | Bajo · estético dentro del archivo |

**Recomendación para empezar**: instala **Extended Graph** (busca en Community plugins). Te da:
- Colores automáticos por carpeta (lessons/=verde, sessions/=azul, lyai-ski/=rojo, etc.)
- Tamaño de nodo proporcional a # de backlinks
- Labels visibles a más zoom-out (en el nativo solo aparecen muy cerca)
- Resaltado de "componentes" conectados al hover

Si quieres algo radicalmente distinto pruebas **Juggl** · te dará un graph tipo Roam/Logseq con layouts profesionales · pero requiere familiarizarse.

Sin plugins · solo CSS snippets también puedes:
- `Settings → Apariencia → CSS snippets` → "Open snippets folder" → crear `graph-custom.css` con reglas para `.graph-view-container` (cambiar fondo, opacidad de links, etc.)

### **Claude** `07:58`

Instalado ✓ (362k descargas · estable aunque sin update reciente · funciona en Obsidian actual igual). Para usarlo:

## Abrir el graph Juggl

**Opción 1 · Command Palette**
- **Ctrl+P** → busca `Juggl` → opciones:
  - `Juggl: Open Juggl` → graph completo del vault
  - `Juggl: Open in workspace` → graph workspace (más enfocado · empiezas desde una nota y vas expandiendo nodos · es el modo recomendado por Juggl)

**Opción 2 · Icon ribbon**
- En el sidebar izquierdo (donde tienes search, bookmarks, etc.) ahora debería haber un icono nuevo de Juggl
- Click ahí

## Modo recomendado para empezar

`Juggl: Open in workspace` es la killer feature:
1. Abres con una nota (ej. `INDEX.md`)
2. El graph muestra solo esa nota + sus 1-hop neighbors
3. Cada nodo es clickable: **shift+click** expande sus neighbors al graph
4. Vas explorando el knowledge graph como un mapa interactivo
5. Layouts disponibles: `cose-bilkent` (organic), `dagre` (hierárquico top-down), `concentric` (radial), `grid`, `circle`, `cola` (force-directed avanzado)

## Configuración inicial sugerida

En **Opciones** del plugin Juggl:
- **Default layout**: `cose-bilkent` (el más estético para empezar)
- **Animate layouts**: ON (transiciones suaves)
- **Style settings**: usar el preset que viene · luego customizas via CSS

## ⚠ Heads-up

Juggl con vault grande (cientos de notas con muchos backlinks) puede tardar 5-10 seg en el primer render del graph completo. Por eso recomienda el workspace mode. Si abres el full graph y se queda colgado: cierra el tab y usa workspace mode mejor.

## Cómo interactuar

| Acción | Resultado |
|---|---|
| **Click** en un nodo | Lo selecciona · te muestra info (en panel lateral) |

| **Mouse wheel** | Zoom in/out |
| **Drag fondo** | Pan (mover toda la vista) |

En el toolbar superior del panel Juggl debería haber selector de layout. Pruébalos uno por uno:
- **cose-bilkent** · orgánico · cluster automático (mi favorito visual)
- **dagre** · top-down hierárquico (bueno si tu wiki tiene jerarquía clara)
- **concentric** · radial · nodo más conectado al centro
- **cola** · force-directed avanzado · físicamente bonito pero pesado
